findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: Every image build executes the shell code returned by the remote URL. If the endpoint or its content is compromised, that code can run with build-stage privileges and alter the resulting image. The URL has no immutable version or integrity check.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: The pipeline returns the exit status of sh, so a curl failure that produces no output can leave sh exiting successfully. The build then continues without running the installer, producing an image that appears successful despite the failed installation.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key error in the public wrapper
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but LoadOrDefault discards that error and returns the same empty string returned for a present key whose value is empty. Public callers cannot distinguish the two cases or handle the failure.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Run previously returned only after every send completed. It now returns as soon as the goroutines are launched, so a caller that closes results after Run returns can cause a send-on-closed-channel panic. A caller that treats return as completion can also stop receiving before the results arrive.

findings.title: Preserve the order of results
findings.whyItBreaks: Each job now sends from an independently scheduled goroutine. For jobs [1, 2], the results can arrive as [4, 2], whereas the previous implementation always sent [2, 4]. Callers associating results with input positions can therefore use the wrong result.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Log function type
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing Log from func(string) to func(string, ...string) preserves direct one-argument calls but changes its function type. Existing clients that assign logger.Log to a func(string) variable or pass it to an API expecting func(string) will fail to compile.

findings.title: Require both administrator status and tenant ownership for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: A non-admin user now passes the deletion check for any record in their tenant, and an admin passes it for records in other tenants. Both cases previously returned false, bypassing the existing authorization and tenant isolation requirements.

findings.title: Propagate settings parsing failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch converts malformed JSON and invalid fields into valid-looking defaults. For example, updateFontSize('{"theme":"dark","fontSize":"14"}', 16, save) now saves a light theme, whereas it previously threw before calling save. Public parseSettings callers also cannot distinguish a parsing failure from legitimate default settings.

findings.title: Retrieve artifacts from the requested branch's commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When the requested branch and the "verified" ref point to different commits, builtFrom identifies the requested branch's commit but artifacts contains the verified commit's artifacts. The new lookup can also fail when the build has no "verified" ref, even if the requested branch exists.

findings.title: Restore the entry limit for positive values
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit, the function returns every entry rather than at most limit entries. For example, renderFeed with 21 entries receives all 21 from recentEntries(all, 20); assigning the 21st item extends its output array, so the feed contains 21 entries.

findings.title: Count only the entries rendered in the manifest
findings.whyItBreaks: The rows exclude stale entries, but the header still uses entries.length. For one stale entry and no live entries, renderManifest emits '# entry-count: 1' with no entry rows, so consumers receive incorrect manifest metadata.

findings.title: Preserve the exported legacy ID formatter
findings.whyItBreaks: FormatLegacyID is an exported Go function. Existing consumers that call it will fail to compile after upgrading, and FormatID cannot produce its LEG-prefixed, ten-digit format.

findings.title: Preserve the shippingQuote export
findings.whyItBreaks: The orders module previously exported shippingQuote, but the replacement only imports quoteShipping for internal use. Existing consumers importing shippingQuote from src/orders will fail to compile or load after upgrading.

findings.title: Reject invalid stored hashes without raising
findings.whyItBreaks: guard(None, 'token', handler) previously returned 401 because the computed string hash did not equal None. compare_digest instead raises TypeError for None; it also raises for a non-ASCII stored string. The guard therefore fails instead of denying the request when a stored hash is missing or malformed.

findings.title: Restore the uppercase result
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call now throws, including execute("hello"), which previously returned "HELLO". Consumers can no longer use the exported function successfully.

findings.title: Allow eligible viewers to reach read-only handling
findings.whyItBreaks: For a request with status "active", role "viewer", and attempts 0, isEligible now returns false, so handle returns "rejected" instead of the previous "read-only" result. The viewer branch in handle is consequently unreachable.

findings.title: Allow unpaid orders to be saved as drafts
findings.whyItBreaks: saveDraft uses the same predicate as submitOrder at src/actions.ts:9. For an order with state "draft" and payment "missing", the new payment check returns false, so saveDraft returns "blocked" instead of "saved". This prevents a user from saving an unfinished order.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the selected channel's head
findings.whyItBreaks: When the requested channel and stable point to different commits, the returned snapshot identifies the requested channel's commit but contains stable's files. Publishing also fails if the stable ref does not exist, even when the requested channel exists.

findings.title: Apply the requested limit when building results
findings.whyItBreaks: The new limit parameter promises to limit the number of results, but the function always iterates 10 times. For example, build('item', limit=2) returns 10 items, exceeding the caller's requested limit.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in the public parser
findings.whyItBreaks: parse_positive_int('-2') returns -2 and parse_positive_int('0') returns 0. Callers of this public function cannot rely on the positivity promised by its name.

findings.title: Preserve the existing public function names
findings.whyItBreaks: Renaming total to total_cents removes total from the module, so existing imports and calls fail. The same change removes read_int at line 1.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame when applying values
findings.whyItBreaks: The assignment now changes the caller's DataFrame in place. Previously, the function updated and returned a copy, so callers could retain the original data. Callers that compare the result with the input or reuse the input after the call will now see their original values overwritten.

findings.title: Enforce the positive integer contract
findings.whyItBreaks: The public name promises a positive integer, but parsing "-2" returns -2 and parsing "0" returns 0. Callers relying on that contract receive non-positive values; charge("-2") consequently returns -200.

findings.title: Preserve the existing public parser symbol
findings.whyItBreaks: Replacing the public read_int function removes an existing API. External code that imports or calls read_int no longer compiles after upgrading.

findings.title: Borrow items in the debug statement
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` takes ownership of the vector. The following `items.len()` then borrows a moved value, causing Rust error E0382 and preventing compilation.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the reported revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The Changeset contract says consumers replay its paths on top of fromRevision, but the paths are now computed from latest. If the pinned tag resolves to revision A and latest resolves to a newer revision B, changes between A and B can be omitted when replaying on A.

findings.title: Update the query when renaming the email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After the migration renames users.email to contact_email, src/query.sql:1 still selects email. Running that query against the migrated schema fails because the column no longer exists.

findings.title: Restore the configured billing API key
findings.whyItBreaks: Every client now receives the committed key instead of BILLING_API_KEY, so deployments cannot use their own credentials or rotate them through configuration. Missing configuration also no longer produces an error. If the committed key is valid, anyone with repository access can use it against the billing API.

findings.title: Restore the administrator check before deleting projects
findings.whyItBreaks: For an archived project, an administrator now receives "forbidden", while a non-admin reaches db.delete(project.id) and receives "purged". The previous implementation allowed deletion only for administrators.

findings.title: Restore the fallback for missing settings
findings.whyItBreaks: When the settings path does not exist, load_settings returns None. Startup now evaluates settings["workers"] and raises TypeError instead of returning the previous default of one worker. A file containing JSON null has the same regression.

findings.title: Return gateway failures to the caller
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge now logs it and returns nil. Callers cannot distinguish a rejected payment from a successful charge and may treat an unpaid transaction as paid. Previously, the gateway error was returned to the caller.

findings.title: Include the tenant ID in the cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A fetches a setting, tenant B requesting the same name receives A's cached value without calling store.fetch. This returns incorrect tenant-specific configuration and can disclose settings across tenants.

findings.title: Preserve the existing invalidation signature
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript callers of invalidate(tenantId, name) no longer type-check. JavaScript callers still pass both arguments, but the function interprets tenantId as the setting name and leaves the intended cached setting in place, causing stale reads.

findings.title: Serialize reservations before awaiting persistence
findings.whyItBreaks: With one unit in stock, two concurrent calls can both read remaining=1 before either save completes. Both then save 0 and return true, so two reservations succeed for one unit. Previously, the stock update completed synchronously before another call could read it.

findings.title: Preserve compatibility for existing Inventory consumers
findings.whyItBreaks: Inventory previously had a zero-argument constructor. Existing TypeScript consumers using new Inventory() now fail to compile; existing JavaScript consumers can construct it but encounter a rejected promise when an in-stock reservation attempts to call save on undefined.

findings.title: Preserve the synchronous reservation contract or version the API
findings.whyItBreaks: reserve previously returned a boolean and now returns a Promise<boolean>. Existing TypeScript callers expecting a boolean fail to compile. JavaScript callers using if (inventory.reserve(sku)) treat the promise as truthy even when the reservation resolves to false, potentially accepting an out-of-stock reservation.

findings.title: Update the retry consumer for millisecond backoff values
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff(0) now returns 1,000 milliseconds, but retry still multiplies it by 1,000 before sleeping at src/jobs/retry.ts:12. The first retry waits 1,000 seconds instead of one second, and the capped delay becomes 30,000 seconds instead of 30 seconds. The sleep also occurs after the final failed attempt, delaying delivery of the error.

findings.title: Propagate errors from closing the output file
findings.whyItBreaks: The deferred Close discards its error. If Flush succeeds but Close reports a delayed write or filesystem error, Save returns nil even though the save failed. Previously, that error was returned to the caller.

findings.title: Include the end of each page window
findings.whyItBreaks: The end bound is already exclusive, so subtracting one omits the last row of every nonempty page. For example, page_window(['a', 'b'], 0, 2) returns ['a']; with a page size of one, every page is empty. render_page and summarize consequently omit rows as well.

findings.title: Preserve the existing public parameter names
findings.whyItBreaks: Renaming public function parameters breaks existing keyword calls. For example, page_window(rows=['a'], page=0, size=1) previously worked but now raises TypeError. The same compatibility break affects clamp(n=..., lo=..., hi=...), page_count(total=..., size=...), render_page(..., page=..., size=...), and summarize(..., size=...).

findings.title: Return cache entries before their TTL expires
findings.whyItBreaks: A lookup before the TTL expires deletes the entry and returns null. If the first lookup happens after the TTL, it returns the expired value and keeps returning it indefinitely.

findings.title: Remove every completed job
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing during forEach shifts the next job into the current index, which forEach then skips. Given two adjacent completed jobs, the second remains in the returned queue.

findings.title: Preserve the input queue when pruning
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported function previously returned a new array and left its argument intact. It now removes elements from the caller's array and returns the same reference, so callers retaining the original queue unexpectedly lose jobs.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before selecting the cutoff
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() without a comparator orders numbers as strings. For players with scores 9 and 10, in that input order, the reversed scores are [9, 10]. With n=1, the cutoff is 9, so topPlayers returns the player scoring 9 instead of the player scoring 10. formatBoard consequently displays the wrong leader.

findings.title: Restore constant-time webhook signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality can take different amounts of time depending on how much of the expected HMAC matches. Repeated verification attempts may expose information about the signature, potentially allowing an attacker to forge one and cause handle() to pass an unauthorized payload to processor.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger insert is committed when the transaction block exits, before either balance update runs. If a balance update fails, the ledger records a transfer that did not complete; if the credit fails after the debit succeeds, the accounts can also be left inconsistent.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when calculating the billing day
findings.whyItBreaks: The local-time getters replace UTC getters. For example, with TZ=America/Los_Angeles, 2024-01-01T00:30:00Z now produces 2023-12-31 instead of 2024-01-01. The same timestamp can therefore receive different billing dates on hosts with different timezones, and sameBillingDay can return a different result near midnight.

findings.title: Include the tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After readProfile('tenant-a', 'alice', ...) caches a profile, readProfile('tenant-b', 'alice', ...) uses the same key and returns tenant-a's profile without calling fetchProfile. This exposes profile data across tenants and returns the wrong tenant's data.

findings.title: Propagate lookup failures instead of returning an empty string
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key previously threw an error; it now returns the same empty string as a key whose stored value is legitimately empty. The catch also suppresses errors thrown by store.get. Consequently, loadAll returns an array containing empty strings where it previously failed, and callers cannot distinguish failed lookups from real values.

findings.title: Preserve compatibility with the existing retry configuration
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript callers that pass { maxAttempts, timeoutMs } no longer satisfy Config. Existing JavaScript callers pass no timeout property, so the deadline becomes NaN and the deadline check never stops retries, although maxAttempts still limits the loop.

findings.title: Report failures from the background retry API
findings.whyItBreaks: If every invocation throws, retryBackground catches the final error and returns void, exactly as it does after a successful invocation. Its public callers have no way to distinguish completed work from work that failed on every attempt.

findings.title: Schedule background retries outside the calling stack
findings.whyItBreaks: The public retryBackground name promises background execution, but it invokes fn synchronously before returning. A slow or blocking callback therefore blocks the caller, and its side effects occur before the caller continues.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading their length
findings.whyItBreaks: The public prop now accepts numbers, but TypeScript rejects value.length because number has no length property. If transpiled without type checking, a numeric value renders as "len=undefined".

findings.title: Preserve the supplied input value
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing callers passing a string now see and submit its length label instead of the supplied value: value="hello" initializes the input to "len=5" instead of "hello".

findings.title: Restore the larger buffer for Git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer reduces the spawnSync output limit from 64 MiB to Node's default of 1 MiB. A PR whose git diff exceeds that limit causes Git to be terminated and git() to throw before review() runs. Patch generation is also outside the try block that posts a failed check, so this path cannot post the review-failure check.

findings.title: Preserve the read-only sandbox for Codex reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: The invocation no longer overrides Codex's sandbox configuration. If Codex is configured with sandbox_mode = "workspace-write" or a less restrictive mode, the agent can modify files in opts.repoPath while processing the supplied prompt. Repository content can influence the agent, so this removes the enforced boundary that previously prevented a review from writing to the repository.

findings.title: Compare from the merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA points to a base branch that has advanced since the PR branched, a direct base-to-HEAD diff includes reversals of base-only changes and can omit PR changes that the base branch independently acquired. The review therefore does not see the pull request's actual changes and can pass a defect that the PR introduced.

findings.title: Diff the configured pull request head
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_HEAD_SHA can differ from the checked-out HEAD, such as when an Actions pull-request checkout uses a synthetic merge commit. The patch now reviews HEAD while the bundle and posted check identify headSha. In particular, a merge commit containing base-branch changes can hide a PR change that was independently made on the base branch, allowing a successful check on a head commit whose actual change was never reviewed.

findings.title: Restore literal replacement for prompt inputs
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing a string as the second argument to String.replace interprets replacement tokens in the input. For example, a patch containing `$$` reaches the critic as `$`, and `$&` becomes `{{PATCH}}`. The same problem affects the serialized bundle and candidate findings. Source text can therefore be changed before review, causing findings to be missed, invented, or incorrectly pruned.

findings.title: Keep the reviewed commit on fallback reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: When the initial review submission fails, the fallback no longer sends commit_id, so GitHub associates the review with the pull request's latest commit. If a new commit was pushed while Needlefish was reviewing the previous head, the fallback presents findings or a change request for the old code as a review of the new commit. The check run is still posted against the original head, so the two results also refer to different commits.

findings.title: Preserve errors for malformed findings
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid or missing severity, category, file and line numbers previously caused normalizeFinding to throw. They now produce ordinary-looking findings: for example, an empty object becomes a P1 bug with an empty file and line 0. normalizeReview returns that finding without any error signal, so callers cannot distinguish malformed review output from a valid finding. Invalid numeric strings can also produce NaN line numbers.

findings.title: Retain the public lenient review mode
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported normalizeReview function previously accepted a second strict argument. TypeScript callers using normalizeReview(raw, false) now fail to compile. JavaScript callers can still pass false, but it is ignored: a null finding now throws during mapping instead of being filtered, aborting the entire review.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection when resolving PR refs
findings.whyItBreaks: A workflow_dispatch event has no pull_request head SHA, so it runs these commands before actions/checkout. Without -R, gh must infer the repository from the current Git checkout. On a clean runner workspace there is no checkout, so both commands fail and write empty outputs. On a self-hosted runner with a stale checkout, they may resolve the same PR number in the wrong repository. The checkout at .github/workflows/review.yml:45 and review inputs at .github/workflows/review.yml:56-57 therefore may not use the requested PR's refs.

findings.title: Reject malformed review output before applying defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported normalizer no longer reports missing or incorrectly typed review fields. For example, a review whose findings field is an object is returned with an empty findings array, indistinguishable from a valid review with no findings. Missing or invalid residual_risks likewise become an empty array, hiding blocking risks. Null input is converted into an entirely empty review. Previously these inputs threw, allowing callers to reject malformed output.

findings.title: Resolve the selected PR's head before checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: A workflow_dispatch event has no pull_request payload, so this checks out github.ref, the branch selected when dispatching the workflow, regardless of pr_number. The workflow then installs and runs the checked-out branch's src/cli.ts at .github/workflows/review.yml:47 instead of the selected PR's code. For example, dispatching from main to review a PR that changes the review tool runs main's tool. The previous step resolved the selected PR's headRefOid before checkout.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer for large diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer reduces spawnSync's limit from 64 MiB to Node's 1 MiB default. When git diff produces more than 1 MiB, spawnSync terminates it and runLocal throws before constructing the review bundle. Diffs between 1 MiB and 64 MiB that previously worked can no longer be reviewed.

findings.title: Keep failed reviews as failing check runs
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub treats a neutral conclusion as satisfying a required status check. If review(), posting the review, or posting the successful check throws, this handler publishes a neutral Needlefish check, so a PR can satisfy that merge requirement even though the review failed. Setting the process exit code does not change the separately published Needlefish check.

findings.title: Bind the reviewed checkout and diff to the same head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR API supplies the current remote head and gh pr diff supplies the current remote diff, but changedFileSet and the review's repoPath still use the existing checkout. If a commit is pushed after the workflow checks out the PR, the review can inspect old files while its review and successful check are posted to the new head. Findings can also be filtered against the old checkout's changed paths.

findings.title: Select the target repository for the PR diff explicitly
findings.whyItBreaks: The metadata request selects GITHUB_REPOSITORY explicitly, but gh pr diff runs in the process working directory without --repo. When runGithub receives a different cwd, or the process directory resolves to another GitHub repository, gh can fail or fetch the same PR number from that other repository. The resulting patch is then reviewed and potentially approved against the target repository's head.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The review command now executes src/cli.ts from the PR head with a token that can write pull requests and checks on a self-hosted runner. A PR can change that code to falsify its own review, exfiltrate the token, or execute arbitrary commands on the runner. The manual dispatch path also permits selecting a fork PR despite the automatic fork restriction.

findings.title: Restore a checkout containing the reviewer
findings.whyItBreaks: The head commit contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json, lockfile, or src/cli.ts. When this PR is reviewed, pnpm install runs in that checkout and cannot install the reviewer, so the review job fails before producing a review. Previously the tool came from a separate frankekn/needlefish checkout.

findings.title: Preserve severity normalization and the conservative fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: A severity such as " p0 " or "p1" previously normalized to P0 or P1, but now fails the exact membership check and becomes P3. Missing or otherwise invalid severities also now become P3 instead of P1. normalizeReview accepts untyped review output and passes each finding through this function, so a serious finding can be returned as a low-priority finding without any indication that its severity was changed.

findings.title: Remove GitHub tokens from the Codex subprocess environment
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an explicit env option, spawnSync passes process.env to Codex, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. A Codex executable or wrapper can now read credentials that were previously excluded. This increases the exposure of credentials when the subprocess is compromised or influenced by untrusted content.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard for the self-hosted review job
findings.whyItBreaks: A pull request from a fork can now run this job after any applicable GitHub Actions approval. The workflow checks out the pull request's head and executes its dependency installation and src/cli.ts on the self-hosted runner. A contributor can therefore execute arbitrary code with the runner's host permissions, exposing local credentials, files, and network access.

findings.title: Preserve zero-duration runner timeout settings
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, setting NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 scheduled SIGKILL immediately after SIGTERM, and setting NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 stopped waiting for inherited pipes immediately after SIGKILL. Both values now select their respective defaults of 5000 ms and 2000 ms, delaying timeout completion and potentially allowing a timed-out process to continue running for five extra seconds.

findings.title: Restore coverage for files outside selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review path selects at most six hotspots and no longer adds a tail hotspot for changed files outside that selection. If the mapper returns a seventh disjoint hotspot or omits a changed file, the file receives no deep review. The critic receives the patch stat on this path, so the review can report a verdict without reviewing the omitted file.

findings.title: Preserve residual risks from each deep review
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep result can contain a blocking residual risk, but the loop keeps only its findings and summary and passes an empty residual_risks array to the critic. A deep reviewer that reports an unresolved blocking issue with no finding has that signal silently erased before the critic can consider it.

findings.title: Preserve the requested focus in large reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: For a patch over 30,000 characters or 10 changed files, reviewLarge no longer includes bundle.focus in the map input or substitutes it into the deep-review prompt. A caller's requested focus therefore does not reach either stage, while small reviews still receive it in the full bundle. If the deep template contains {{FOCUS}}, that marker is also left unresolved.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported parsePositiveInteger function promises a positive integer, but it now returns 0 for "0". It also returns 0 for an empty or whitespace-only string because Number converts those inputs to zero. Callers relying on this parser for positive values receive an invalid value instead of the previous error.
